examples.en: I am very ticklish.
Please don't tickle the soles of my feet.
I couldn't stop laughing because of the tickling.
The baby giggles at the tickle.
I felt a tickle on my neck and turned around.
My older sister isn't ticklish at all.

explain: '간지럼을 타다'는 쉽게 간지러움을 느낀다는 뜻이고, '간지럼을 태우다'는 남을 간지럽게 하는 뜻이라서 구분해야 해요. '간지러움'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만 대화에서는 '간지럼'이 더 흔해요.
explain_en: Keep '간지럼을 타다' (to be ticklish) apart from '간지럼을 태우다' (to tickle someone). '간지러움' has the same meaning, but '간지럼' is more common in conversation.

examples.ko: 머리가 아플 때 관자놀이를 눌러 줘요.
examples.en: When I have a headache, I press my temples.
The area around my temples was throbbing, so I took medicine.
When he got nervous, sweat formed on his temples.
My glasses are too tight and my temples hurt.

examples.ko: 거울을 보니 관자놀이 쪽 머리가 세기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Looking in the mirror, I saw the hair at my temples starting to go gray.
He got angry and the veins at his temples stood out.

explain: 눈과 귀 사이, 옆머리 쪽 부분이에요. 머리가 아플 때 '관자놀이가 지끈거리다', '관자놀이가 욱신거리다'처럼 아픈 느낌과 함께 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the area at the side of the head between the eye and the ear. It often appears with pain words, as in '관자놀이가 지끈거리다' or '관자놀이가 욱신거리다' when you have a headache.

examples.ko: 회사에는 굽이 낮은 단화를 신고 가요.
examples.en: I wear low-heeled flats to the office.

examples.ko: 단화는 편해서 많이 걸어도 발이 안 아파요.
examples.en: Flat shoes are comfortable, so my feet don't hurt even after a lot of walking.

examples.ko: 검은 단화 한 켤레를 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a new pair of black flat shoes.
Flat shoes go well with both skirts and pants.

examples.ko: 이 단화는 끈이 없어서 신고 벗기 쉬워요.
examples.en: These flat shoes have no laces, so they're easy to put on and take off.
It rained, and my flat shoes got soaked.

explain: 발목 아래까지만 오는 굽 낮은 신발이에요. 부츠처럼 목이 긴 신발과 달리 발등이 많이 드러나요. 운동화와는 달리 정장이나 단정한 옷차림에 신는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a low-heeled shoe that comes only up to the ankle. Unlike long-shafted boots, much of the top of the foot shows. Unlike sneakers, it is often worn with formal or neat outfits.

examples.en: The child spins round and round on the spot.
A helicopter is circling in the sky.
My head was spinning, so I sat down for a moment.

examples.ko: 길을 몰라서 같은 곳을 빙빙 돌았어요.
examples.en: I didn't know the way, so I went around the same place again and again.

examples.ko: 이야기가 빙빙 돌기만 하고 결론이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The talk just goes around in circles with no conclusion.
Birds are flying in circles above the tree.

explain: '빙빙 돌다'로 가장 많이 써요. 작은말 '뱅뱅'은 작고 가벼운 것에, '빙빙'은 그보다 큰 느낌에 써요. 어지러울 때 '머리가 빙빙 돌다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 말을 빙빙 돌리지 말고 핵심부터 말해 주세요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하고 싶은 말을 바로 하지 않고 돌려서 말한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: To avoid saying what you mean directly and talk around it.

explain_en: The most common pattern is '빙빙 돌다'. The smaller-sounding '뱅뱅' fits small, light things, while '빙빙' feels bigger. When you're dizzy you can say '머리가 빙빙 돌다'.

examples.en: I get diarrhea when I drink cold milk.
I had diarrhea all night yesterday.
When a baby has diarrhea, we go to the hospital.
I drank a lot of water while I had diarrhea.
I had diarrhea all day and a fever too.
I ate spoiled food and had diarrhea, so it was hard.

explain: '설사를 하다'로 띄어 쓸 수도 있어요. 병원에서는 '배탈이 났어요'라고도 말하는데, 배탈은 설사뿐 아니라 배가 아픈 증상 전체에 써요.
explain_en: You can also split it as '설사를 하다'. People also say '배탈이 났어요', and '배탈' covers stomach trouble in general, not only diarrhea.

examples.en: Morning sickness makes every morning hard for me.

examples.ko: 언니는 입덧이 심해서 음식을 잘 못 먹어요.
examples.en: My sister has severe morning sickness and can hardly eat.

examples.ko: 친구는 입덧을 할 때 귤만 먹었대요.
examples.en: My friend says she only ate tangerines when she had morning sickness.

examples.ko: 입덧에 좋은 음식이 있으면 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If there is food that helps with morning sickness, please tell me.

examples.ko: 임신 초기에는 입덧으로 고생하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people suffer from morning sickness in early pregnancy.
Morning sickness differs from person to person, so don't worry.

explain: '입덧을 하다', '입덧이 심하다'처럼 써요. 속이 울렁거리는 일반 증상은 '멀미'나 '메스꺼움'이라고 하고, 입덧은 임신했을 때만 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '입덧을 하다' or '입덧이 심하다'. A general queasy feeling is 멀미 or 메스꺼움, while 입덧 is only for pregnancy.

examples.ko: 어제 먹은 음식 때문에 장염에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I got enteritis from something I ate yesterday.
I have enteritis, so I could not go to work today.
The doctor said it was enteritis.

examples.ko: 장염에 걸리면 죽을 먹는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When you have enteritis, it is good to eat porridge.
Enteritis is going around among the children.
I suffered for two days because of enteritis.

explain: '장염'은 설사와 복통이 나고 열이 날 때도 있는, 배탈보다 심한 병이에요. 가볍게 배가 아픈 것은 '배탈'이라고 하고, 병원에서 진단을 받았을 때 '장염'이라고 말해요. '장염에 걸리다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: 장염 is a more serious illness than 배탈, with diarrhea and stomach pain, and sometimes fever. A mild stomachache is 배탈, and you say 장염 when a doctor has diagnosed it. The common phrase is 장염에 걸리다.

examples.en: My child's baby tooth was loose, so we went to the dentist.

examples.ko: 젖니는 빠지고 나면 새 이가 나요.
examples.en: After a baby tooth falls out, a new tooth grows in.
My daughter had her first baby tooth pulled.
Baby teeth can get cavities too.

examples.ko: 젖니 때부터 양치하는 습관을 들여야 해요.
examples.en: You should build the habit of brushing from the baby-teeth stage.

examples.ko: 젖니에 구멍이 생기면 치과에 가야 해요.
examples.en: If a baby tooth gets a hole, you need to go to the dentist.

explain: 병원에서는 '유치'라고도 하고, 일상에서는 '젖니'라고 많이 말해요. 반대말은 평생 쓰는 '간니'(영구치)예요. 발음은 [전니]예요. 받침 'ㅈ'이 'ㄷ' 소리가 되고, 뒤의 'ㄴ' 때문에 다시 'ㄴ'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: At the dentist it is also called '유치', and in daily talk people say '젖니'. The opposite is '간니' (permanent tooth). It is pronounced [전니]: the final 'ㅈ' becomes a 'ㄷ' sound, and because of the following 'ㄴ' it then changes to 'ㄴ'.

examples.en: My head was throbbing, so I took medicine.

examples.ko: 어제 잠을 못 자서 아침부터 머리가 지끈거려요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep yesterday, so my head has been pounding since morning.

examples.ko: 머리가 지끈거리는 걸 보니 감기에 걸렸나 봐요.
examples.en: My head is pounding, so I think I caught a cold.
My head throbbed because of the loud noise.
The throbbing headache has gotten a little better.
If your forehead throbs, rest for a moment.

explain: 머리가 계속 욱신거리며 아플 때 '머리가 지끈거려요'라고 자주 말해요. '머리가 아파요'보다 둔하게 쑤시는 느낌이 있어요. 주어는 보통 아픈 부위(머리, 이마)예요.
explain_en: People often say '머리가 지끈거려요' when their head pounds continuously. Compared with '머리가 아파요', it has a dull, throbbing feel. The subject is usually the aching part, like 머리 or 이마.

examples.en: I was in a hurry and went out wearing mismatched socks.
I didn't know my shoes were mismatched.
I wore mismatched earrings on purpose.
The child wearing mismatched gloves was cute.

examples.ko: 아침에 옷을 짝짝이로 입고 와서 친구들이 웃었어요.
examples.en: I came dressed in mismatched clothes this morning, and my friends laughed.

examples.ko: 눈 크기가 짝짝이라서 사진 찍을 때 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: My eyes are different sizes, so I worry about it when taking photos.

explain: 양말, 신발, 장갑처럼 짝이 맞아야 하는 두 개가 서로 다르게 된 것을 말해요. 눈이나 귀처럼 양쪽이 비대칭인 모습에도 쓰고, 보통 '짝짝이로 신다/하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It means two things that should match, such as socks, shoes or gloves, are different from each other. It is also used for uneven pairs like eyes or ears, and usually appears as '짝짝이로 신다/하다'.
